sbh2.5:1.1: What is the analysis of elements?
sbh2.5:1.3: the earth element, water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element.
sbh2.5:2.3: The inward earth element: whatever in this body, internally, individually, is hard or harsh, has come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:2.4: The outward earth element: whatever externally is hard, has gone to hardness, has not come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:2.5: What, further, is the inward earth element?
sbh2.5:2.6: Hair of the head, body hair, nails, teeth, dust, dirt, skin, flesh, bone, sinew, vein, kidneys, heart, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery;
sbh2.5:2.9: liver, feces. This is called the inward earth element.
sbh2.5:2.10: What, further, is the outward earth element?
sbh2.5:2.11: Wood, clods, gravel, potsherds, trees, mountain-peaks — and anything else of this kind. This is called the outward earth element.
sbh2.5:3.4: What is the inward water element?
sbh2.5:3.5: Whatever, internally, individually, is moist or has gone to moistness,
sbh2.5:3.6: is water, has gone to the water element, has come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:3.9: fat, lymph, marrow, grease, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, brain, brain-membrane, urine. This is called the inward water element.
sbh2.5:3.10: What is the outward water element?
sbh2.5:3.11: Whatever externally is water, has gone to water, is moist, has gone to moistness, has not come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:3.12: Springs, lakes, ponds, rivers, fountains — and anything else of this kind. This is called the outward water element.
sbh2.5:4.2: The fire element is twofold: inward and outward.
sbh2.5:4.3: What is the inward fire element?
sbh2.5:4.4: Whatever, internally, individually, is fire or heat, has gone to fire or heat, has come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:4.5: Namely: the fire in this body by which the body is heated,
sbh2.5:4.7: by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted goes to proper digestion with ease;
sbh2.5:4.8: and through whose excess one comes to be reckoned [Conjectural: ‘feverish’].
sbh2.5:4.9: What is the outward fire element?
sbh2.5:4.10: Whatever externally is fire or heat, has gone to fire or heat, has not come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:4.11: That which people seek from fire-sticks and cow-dung powder;
sbh2.5:4.12: that which, having arisen, burns even a village,
sbh2.5:4.14: a city, part of a city, a country, part of a country, an island, a thicket, a forest, wood, grass, or cow-dung — burning these, it goes on.
sbh2.5:4.15: And anything else of this kind. [Lacuna]
sbh2.5:5.5: whatever, internally, individually, is wind or has gone to wind —
sbh2.5:5.6: that which is lightness, motion, come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:5.7: Furthermore, in this body there are: upward-going winds, downward-going winds, side-resting winds;
sbh2.5:5.13: winds following the limbs and minor limbs.
sbh2.5:5.14: What is the outward wind element?
sbh2.5:5.15: Whatever externally is wind or has gone to wind — that lightness and motion,
sbh2.5:5.16: not come to be taken up.
sbh2.5:5.17: There are externally: eastern winds, southern winds,
sbh2.5:5.19: dust-bearing winds, dustless winds, small winds, great winds, *viśva* winds, *vairambha* winds, wind-circle winds.
sbh2.5:5.20: There is a time when a great mass of wind has accumulated and topples even tree-tops,
sbh2.5:5.23: having toppled them, with nothing to sustain it, it dies away.
sbh2.5:5.24: There are beings who seek [wind] with a corner of the robe, a palm-leaf, or a fan.
sbh2.5:5.25: Such wind, and anything else of this kind. [Lacuna]
sbh2.5:6.2: The cavities of the eye, ear, nose, mouth, and throat;
sbh2.5:6.5: that through which what is ingested passes;
sbh2.5:6.6: that through which it flows out below;
sbh2.5:6.7: and anything else of this kind. This is called the space element.
sbh2.5:7.2: Eye-consciousness; ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, mind-consciousness;
sbh2.5:7.3: That, further, is mind, [Conjectural: mentality, and consciousness].
sbh2.5:7.4: This is called the consciousness element.
sbh2.5:8.1: The conceit-conduct person, attending to this analysis of elements, dispels the perception of the body as a unified lump.
sbh2.5:8.2: He also obtains the perception of unattractiveness;
sbh2.5:8.3: and no longer becomes elevated [proud] through [the body].
sbh2.5:8.5: and purifies the mind from conceit-conduct.
sbh2.5:8.6: This is called the analysis of elements —
sbh2.5:8.7: the conduct-purifying object for the conceit-conduct person.
